timelineEvents.title: Transfer to the Staszic Real School
timelineEvents.label: 1915 · Skrynnikov school graduation
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Aged thirteen, Kaper moved from Skrynnikov’s private school to the fifth class of the Staszic Real School in Warsaw, in the school year that began under the new German occupation.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper attended the private school of Aleksander M. Skrynnikov at 49 Żurawia Street, whose curriculum favoured mathematics, the sciences and modern languages over the classical programme of Latin and Greek. Aged thirteen, he transferred to the fifth class of the Stanisław Staszic Real School, which became a state gymnasium in 1918 and where he completed his secondary education. The transfer is placed in the 1915/16 school year rather than on a day, and the reason is what happened to Warsaw schooling that summer: in July 1915 the Russian state and private secondary schools of the city were evacuated into Russia with their staff, most of their pupils and their classroom equipment, and the German army took the school buildings when it entered Warsaw on 5 August. Schooling was then rebuilt through the autumn by the education department of the Citizens’ Committee, which resolved to organise compulsory teaching only on 23 August and was still forming school divisions in November. No source consulted here gives a day for the move.
